extension.summary: tofa media server: user interface, plus a browsable video source
extension.description:
An unofficial client for the tofa media server (tofa.tv), in two parts.
Under Programs, tofa opens a full user interface: Home, Browse, Discover, Search, title detail with cast and episodes, its own player chrome, and Settings.
Under Video add-ons, the same library appears as a browsable source, so it can also be used in widgets, favourites and Kodi's own containers.
Both play through Kodi's native VideoPlayer, negotiating DirectPlay/DirectFile so Dolby Vision, TrueHD/DTS-HD passthrough and refresh-rate matching reach it untouched.
extension.disclaimer: An unofficial tofa client, engineered with the tofa team, who also help support it.
extension.news: - You can re-arrange your Home screen. Settings > Appearance gives every row its own controls: move it up, move it down, switch it off, or take it off the list if you put it there yourself. The ten rows every tofa account starts with can be switched off but not removed, which is how tofa's other apps behave. Adding a row is now one control listing everything you can add, grouped into Discover lists, genres and Home rows. - If your Home screen has ten rows, the tenth one is now there. The add-on had room for nine, so the last row simply did not appear, and could not be reached in Settings either. A tofa account now starts with ten rows, so this affected anyone who had not changed theirs. - Settings that offer a few fixed choices now show all of them at once, so you can go straight to the one you want instead of stepping through the others. This covers the rating badge, preferred quality, whether to play the next episode, and the five skip behaviours. - An episode's own title now appears on the detail screen, at the start of the line carrying the year and the rest of the details. - The note under the Home screen row list showed a stray line of text belonging to Kodi's skin instead of tofa's own wording.
